entries.descriptionOriginal: A clean, fair and fast 1v1 aim arena built for competitive duels. About An industrial yard arena designed exclusively for ONNSKINS 1v1 (X1) matches. Two teams spawn at opposite ends of a large open yard with cover in the middle: crates, barrels, containers and two white canisters that break the straight line of sight. The layout is symmetrical, so neither side has an advantage. Symmetrical layout: equal angles, lighting and cover for both sides Large yard (about 2400 x 1600 units) with several routes: left, center and right Built for 1v1 duels and aim practice Lightweight and optimized for high FPS (small addon, simple lighting, no heavy effects) No weapons, items or buy zones in the map: weapons are set by the server Clean visuals with good enemy visibility /list Game modes 1v1 / Deathmatch Aim practice Custom Used on ONNSKINS X1: skin duels with real matches. onnskins.com.br Tips Use the central canisters to break the line of sight before peeking Control the lateral lanes to flank without being seen Made by ONNSKINS. Feedback and suggestions are welcome in the comments.

entries.descriptionOriginal: Welcome to My First Map London's West End on a wet night: Piccadilly Circus, the four streets that meet there, the back alleys behind them, and a Tube station underneath that you can play in. This is the bomb defusal version. The deathmatch version is here: London – Piccadilly Circus (Deathmatch). Watch the trailer on YouTube Bomb defusal Spawns: Terrorists start in Brewer Street mews, the back alley on the north side. Counter-Terrorists start in St James's mews on the south side. Bombsite A: the Criterion arcade, with doors from the Circus, Coventry Street and Haymarket. Bombsite B: the building site behind the old facade, with gates from Piccadilly and Haymarket, and a scaffold walkway that looks out over the Circus. Mid: the Circus round Eros. The Tube runs underneath and links the two halves of the map. Both sites have big stencilled letters on a wall and on the floor, and arrows on the old facade point the way to B. Bots can play it: they buy and plant at both sites. What's in the map Piccadilly Circus at night: the curved Lights screen, the Shaftesbury Memorial Fountain (Eros) in the middle, and gulls circling overhead. Four streets: Regent Street, Coventry Street, Haymarket and Piccadilly, with street name plates, zebra crossings, Belisha beacons and a red bus lane on Regent Street. London street life: Routemaster buses, black cabs, a police car, red phone boxes, pillar boxes, bus shelters, newspaper kiosks, an ice-cream kiosk and a food stall. Buildings you can go into: a gift shop under the Lights; the Eros Arms pub, with a room upstairs whose bay windows look over the Circus (they break when shot); the Criterion arcade with its gold mosaic ceiling; and the building site. Chinatown: a lane hung with red lanterns, lit shopfronts, and the Lucky Star supermarket, which you can walk into. Back alleys: a ring of service alleys round the outside of the map, with bins, pallets and containers for cover and 35 pieces of graffiti on the walls. The Underground: four stairways from the Circus lead down to a ticket hall with ticket barriers, ticket machines and a ticket office. Working escalators, one up and one down, link the hall and the platforms, where a three-car train stands with its doors open: walk through it to the far platform. Push-button lifts at both ends of the platforms go up to the back alleys. Weather: rain, wet roads and night fog. Down in the Tube it stays dry. Radar: the minimap shows the streets, and switches to the Tube level when you go underground. How to play offline with bots Press Subscribe on this page. Steam downloads the map. In CS2, go to Play, then Workshop Maps, and pick London – Piccadilly Circus (Bomb Defusal). Choose Casual or Competitive as the game mode if asked, then press Go. To add bots, open the console and type bot_quota 10 (or any number). bot_kick removes them. The console is turned on under Settings > Game > Enable Developer Console; the key under Esc opens it. You can also start the map straight from the console (Casual; use game_mode 1 for Competitive): game_type 0; game_mode 0; host_workshop_map 3828557718 Credits Map by Zen. Models used under CC BY 4.0: Phone box: "London Phone Booth" by stovepipe (Sketchfab, CC BY 4.0). Bus: "Routemaster Bus" and cab: "LTI TX4 London Taxi" by Nieve5677 (Sketchfab, CC BY 4.0). Street lamp: "Victorian Street Lamp" by Rosbergen Designs (Sketchfab, CC BY 4.0). Police car: "Ford Focus British Police Car, UK" by David_Holiday (Sketchfab, CC BY 4.0). Traffic light: "UK Traffic Light | Game Ready | Low Poly" by ThomasRedfern12 (Sketchfab, CC BY 4.0). All modified for CS2. Model pages: Phone Booth, Routemaster Bus, TX4 Taxi, Street Lamp, Police Car, Traffic Light. Licence: CC BY 4.0. Found a bug, or a spot where you get stuck? Tell me in the comments. This is a fan-made map and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Transport for London or any brand shown.
